# Results — Study 536 (Anomaly-Decay-Post-Publication) on a survivor basket

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). A McLean & Pontiff (2016)
publication-decay reckoning run as a battery: four classic cross-sectional anomalies
(12-1 momentum, low volatility, 1-month reversal, 3-year reversal), each rebuilt as a
price-only top-tercile-minus-bottom-tercile long-short on a fixed 40-name large-cap
survivor basket, then SPLIT at the anomaly's academic publication year — the mean
return before vs after. As-of **2026-05** (the last full month — the in-progress June
bars are dropped); match the fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Universe | 40-name large-cap **survivor** basket, monthly total return |
| Window | 1980-02 → 2026-05 (556 months, 40 names) |
| Fingerprint | `d7fbd2229df0` |
| Source | Yahoo! Finance auto-adjusted daily closes → month-end total returns (`yfinance`) |
| Anomalies | 12-1 momentum (pub. 1993), low-vol (2006), 1-month reversal (1990), 3-year reversal (1985) |

> **Survivorship — named, not hidden.** Every name still trades in 2026, so the *level*
> of each anomaly is biased (survivors are the winners). The study's quantity of
> interest is the *within-anomaly pre/post ratio*, which the survivorship tilt enters on
> **both** sides — but the absolute returns below should not be read as a deployable edge.
> Opt-in guard: a point-in-time index-membership basket would lower the levels; the decay
> *pattern* is the robust finding.

## The headline — anomalies shrink after they are published

| Anomaly | Published | Pre ann. (t) | Post ann. (t) | Decay (post/pre) | Placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **12-1 momentum** | 1993 | **+14.79% (t=3.14)** | +3.66% (t=1.11) | **0.25 (−75%)** | **0.039** |
| 1-month reversal | 1990 | +9.16% (t=1.93) | +0.18% (t=0.07) | **0.02 (−98%)** | 0.054 |
| 3-year reversal | 1985 | +7.16% (t=0.80) | +2.67% (t=1.09) | 0.37 (−63%) | 0.343 |
| low volatility | 2006 | −11.38% (t=−2.79) | −9.60% (t=−2.50) | 0.84 (−16%) | 0.630 |
| **Median** | — | — | — | **0.31** | — |

- **Momentum is the textbook case.** Pre-1993 the 12-1 momentum long-short earned
  **+14.8%/yr at t = 3.14** — comfortably real. Post-1993 it earns **+3.7%/yr at t = 1.11**,
  *below the t ≥ 2 bar*. The post/pre ratio is **0.25** and the label-shuffle placebo says a
  drop this large appears by chance only **3.9%** of the time. The anomaly did not vanish, but
  it more than halved — exactly the McLean-Pontiff prediction.
- **Short-term reversal all but disappears.** Pre-1990 t = 1.93 → post-1990 t = 0.07; the
  post mean is essentially zero (ratio 0.02). At an average turnover of **0.67/month** this was
  never tradable net of costs anyway, but the *decay* is stark (placebo *p* = 0.054).
- **The median decay ratio is 0.31** — *more* shrinkage than the ~0.50 McLean-Pontiff
  average, which is unsurprising on a small survivor basket where the pre-publication
  numbers are themselves inflated by the survivors' winning streak.

## The low-vol caveat (an honest non-result)

Low-vol is the one anomaly that does **not** decay here — but only because on this basket
it is *negative* in both halves (long-low-vol / short-high-vol **loses** ~10%/yr). On a
mega-cap survivor basket the "low-vol anomaly" inverts: the high-vol names (NVDA, the
mega-cap winners) *are* the survivors that ran. So there is no positive edge to decay. We
report it rather than drop it; it is a clean reminder that a survivor basket distorts every
anomaly's *level* (see the survivorship note).

## Net of costs — nothing survives to deploy

One-way **10 bps/leg × turnover** + **50 bps/yr borrow** on the short leg:

| Anomaly | Post-publication GROSS ann. | Post-publication NET ann. | Net post *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 12-1 momentum | +3.66% | **+2.69%** | +0.82 |
| 1-month reversal | +0.18% | **−1.92%** | −0.73 |
| 3-year reversal | +2.67% | +1.85% | +0.75 |
| low volatility | −9.60% | −10.35% | −2.70 |

Every positive post-publication leg falls **below t = 2 net of costs**; the only
statistically-strong net leg is low-vol's *negative* one. There is no deployable edge here —
the study is about *decay*, not a tradable signal.

## Synthetic positive control — the split engine is faithful

A deterministic panel with a PLANTED anomaly whose strength steps down at a "publication"
month (20-seed averaged, so no single lucky RNG seed drives it):

| Planted post-decay | Expected ratio | Recovered ratio | Pre *t* | Post *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 (no decay) | 1.00 | **+0.984** | +16.31 | +15.87 |
| 0.5 (half — McLean-Pontiff) | 0.50 | **+0.495** | +16.29 | +8.01 |
| 1.0 (full decay — the null) | 0.00 | **+0.004** | +16.26 | +0.08 |

The engine recovers the planted pre/post step to two decimals, and at full decay the post
leg is statistically dead (t = 0.08) — a faithful detector that cannot manufacture a decay
where none was planted, nor hide one that was. **This is a power/faithfulness check only;
it is never cited to support a real-tape stamp.**

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** This is a methodology demo, not an anomaly hunt. The momentum decay is
  real (placebo *p* = 0.039) but the *point* is that the post-publication leg falls **below
  t = 2** — i.e. the signal *erodes*. No new tradable edge is claimed; the survivor basket
  inflates the pre-publication numbers it leans on.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net of costs every positive post-publication leg is sub-t = 2
  (momentum +2.7%/yr at t = 0.82), and the highest-turnover anomaly (reversal, 0.67/mo) goes
  negative. The pre-publication "edge" you would have wanted to trade is exactly the part that
  decayed away — a textbook mirage.
- **Do anomalies decay after publication? — CONFIRMED.** Median post/pre ratio **0.31** across
  four classic anomalies; momentum −75% (placebo *p* = 0.039), short-term reversal −98%. The
  McLean-Pontiff ~50% half-life shows up even on a tiny survivor basket — if anything stronger,
  because the survivors' pre-publication run is the most over-stated half.
